description: Auckland Council publishes 22 stormwater layers of Auckland Council covering pipes, manholes and chambers, catchpits, inlets and outlets, channels, watercourses, connections, pump stations, dams, spillways, embankments, treatment devices and facilities, soakage systems, septic tanks, forebays, planting, safety benching, fences, erosion and flood control structures, viewing platforms and a stormwater management area control overlay. Coverage: the Auckland region (New Zealand); the layers were last modified on 2026-09-25 according to the hub. Format and access: CSV, shapefile, GeoJSON and KML downloads plus ArcGIS REST feature services, without registration from the Auckland Council open data hub. Licence (read on the portal page on 2026-09-29): CC BY 4.0; cost: free. Caveats: the description says seven legacy systems were migrated into the council GIS and that the data are indicative and cannot be aligned to cadastral or other boundaries; asset counts, ages and attribute fields were not read; private drains and other networks (wastewater, water supply) are not in these layers. Simulation uses: stormwater network topology for urban flood and drainage models, pipe and pump-station capacity and criticality studies, and cascading-failure analysis with roads and wastewater systems. Related catalogue records: OpenStreetMap (data-openstreetmap).
